prize_parts.citation: For visionary, densely patterned prose and poetry that build a metaphysical architecture out of memory, the body and dream.

statement.case_for: On the common criteria, B043 gives the clearest combination of a recognizable voice, formal ambition and a project that accumulates across the oeuvre. From public knowledge, the Orbitor trilogy (Blinding) and Solenoid build large, recursive structures from childhood memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation. I read this as one sustained undertaking rather than a single peak. The late novels extend the earlier ones instead of repeating them, and the poetry and shorter prose appear to be the lyric and miniature roots of the same imaginative system. The voice is a test I take seriously: it should be audible in the writing and nowhere else on the list. Scale and stylistic singularity coincide here, which is rare. The citation scope is clean, with one writer and one language, and the fiction and poetry can be covered by one formulation. My opening reading is unchanged after reconsidering colleagues' arguments, and some of those arguments sharpen my reservations.
statement.case_against: My strongest reservation is that the case depends on prose density, rhythm and sentence-level control in Romanian, which I can judge only through translations and critical accounts. Some of the long, digressive books may be excessive, and quality across the whole corpus may be uneven. The inward, maximalist mode may also be narrower in its significance than its scale suggests. Coverage of the poetry and early work in translation is thinner, so a citation that names poetry would rest on weaker evidence than one resting on the novels. I have not independently verified the texts, and my assessment rests on public knowledge.

responses.point: Olsson ranked Anne Carson first for an unmistakable voice and formal invention joining classical scholarship, lyric, essay and book-object form. He also noted that the corpus is modest in scale and that classical allusion and typographic design may not survive translation. He ranked Cărtărescu second.
responses.response: I agree that Carson's voice is unmistakable and that Autobiography of Red and Nox show real formal invention and intellectual depth. I did not place her in my own top eight, and I hold that placement loosely. My knowledge of her work is narrower than my knowledge of the other candidates, so I would not claim to have weighed her fully. The reservations Olsson himself lists are the ones that keep me from moving her first. A large part of the oeuvre consists of translations, adaptations and occasional pieces, so the weight of the original achievement must be argued from a few landmark books. Some of the effect depends on the printed object, which a committee reading text cannot assess. On sustained quality across a body of work, Cărtărescu's cumulative project seems to me the easier case to make. I would still want the committee to examine the Carson case carefully rather than settle it through genre assumptions.

responses.point: Sward ranked Cărtărescu first but flagged that the inward, maximalist mode may limit the breadth of significance claimed. She ranked Carson last on her list, questioning how hybrid, between-category work fits the will's wording on literary work.
responses.response: The breadth concern is fair, and I share part of it. Cărtărescu's mode is deliberately inward, and I cannot show from public knowledge that its significance extends equally across all registers. What I can say is that the project moves between bodily, autobiographical, grotesque, comic and speculative material and between verse and prose. That is more variety than a narrow label suggests, though I hold this with caution. On Carson, I would separate two questions. Hybridity as such seems to me no obstacle under the will. The open question is how much of the oeuvre is original literary work and how much is translation and scholarship. I would not use genre boundaries alone to exclude a writer.

responses.point: Palm ranked Michon third, praising the formal precision and consistency of his compressed prose. She treated the slim volume of work as a question of breadth rather than durability.
responses.response: I agree with that distinction and ranked Michon second for the same reasons. Vies minuscules, Les Onze and the other books show a rigorous, unmistakable French prose with a distinct method for imagining lost lives and artistic vocation. Where I differ is on how far consistency can substitute for range. A small, concentrated body of work can be a complete achievement, but I find the breadth and sustained-quality criteria easier to satisfy for Cărtărescu. That is why I treat Michon as an alternative rather than my first choice. Translation losses matter more for Michon, because his effect lies in syntax and register. The committee would need to read him in French or accept a partial judgment.

responses.point: Carlberg ranked Cărtărescu first and Adonis second. She cautioned that the length and encyclopedic density of the novels may divide readers' judgments of sustained quality. She also noted that her knowledge of his poetry and essays is thinner than her knowledge of the novels.
responses.response: Both cautions apply to my own assessment. Density may count as depth or as excess, and I cannot settle that for every volume. I also agree that the poetry coverage is thinner, so I would build a citation mainly on the prose and mention poetry only if the committee can read enough of it. On Adonis, I share Carlberg's attention to the limits of translation for Arabic prosody and her refusal to weigh political stances as literary evidence. His reshaping of Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and dialogue with the classical tradition is a major formal achievement. That is why he remains my alternative for the poetic strand.

uncertainties: How much of Cărtărescu's stylistic achievement survives translation, and whether the long, digressive books sustain quality throughout.
How thoroughly the committee can read his poetry and early prose, since translated coverage is thinner than for the novels.

Whether Carson's original literary achievement is large enough, relative to her translations and scholarship, to carry a whole-oeuvre citation. My own knowledge of her work is narrower than for other candidates.
Whether Michon's small corpus and Adonis's Arabic prosody can be judged adequately in translation.
All judgments here rest on general public knowledge and translated or reported evidence, not on independent verification of texts.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. It records no personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted writer.
